A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the institutional theory of corporate behavior offers a framework for understanding how and why corporations behave in ways that are not dictated by the market.
we find that corporations behave in socially responsible way when they have to, when they want to, and when they are able to.
we have found that the institutional conditions are important in explaining why some corporations behave in socially responsible and others do not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
corporations are not likely to behave in a socially responsible way if they are left to their own devices.
corporations are not likely to behave in a socially responsible manner unless they are subject to a variety of institutional pressures to do so.
corporate social responsibility is not a matter of the market, but a function of the institutions of society.
